telescope_optics.goal: A telescope collects starlight over a round mirror of diameter D; your eye collects it through a pupil of diameter p. Write G, how many times more light the telescope gathers.
telescope_optics.name: Aperture gain
telescope_optics.ask: Find G for a 2.4 m mirror against a dark-adapted pupil of 7 mm (0.007 m).

vars.G: light gathered, relative to the eye

telescope_optics.method: Light collected is proportional to the collecting area, π(D/2)², so the ratio of two apertures is the square of the ratio of their diameters.

meteoritics.goal: A body of mass m strikes the ground at speed v. All of its motion becomes heat, shock and a crater. Write the energy E it brings.
meteoritics.name: Kinetic energy of an impactor
meteoritics.ask: Find E in terajoules for the body that made Meteor Crater: m = 3e8 kg at v = 12800 m/s.
meteoritics.method: The work needed to bring a mass from rest to speed v is the integral of m·v dv, which is half of m v².

stellar_astrophysics.goal: A star is a ball of radius R whose surface glows at temperature T. Every square metre of a perfect radiator gives off σT⁴. Write the star's total power L.
stellar_astrophysics.name: Stefan-Boltzmann law for a star
stellar_astrophysics.ask: Find L for the Sun, in units of 10²⁶ W: R = 6.96e8 m, T = 5772 K, s = 5.67e-8 W/(m²·K⁴).
stellar_astrophysics.method: Multiply the power per square metre by the area of the sphere, 4πR².

radio_astronomy.goal: A cloud of hydrogen emits a line at frequency ν _ 0. Moving away from us at speed v, it is received at a lower frequency ν. For speeds far below light's, write v.
radio_astronomy.name: Radial velocity from the line shift
radio_astronomy.ask: Find v in km/s for the 21 cm line, A = 1420.406 MHz, received at B = 1420.000 MHz (c = 299792 km/s).
radio_astronomy.method: Each successive wave crest is emitted v/c of a wavelength further away, so the received frequency drops by the fraction v/c.

galactic_dynamics.goal: A cloud of gas circles the centre of a galaxy at radius r, held by the gravity of the mass M inside its orbit. Write the speed v it must have to stay on a circle.
galactic_dynamics.name: Circular orbital speed
galactic_dynamics.ask: Find v in km/s for the Sun's orbit: M = 1.8e41 kg within r = 2.5e20 m, G = 6.674e-11.
galactic_dynamics.method: Gravity supplies exactly the centripetal force: G M m / r² = m v² / r.
